snippet: Tong Hsing Electronic Industries (THEIL), a semiconductor packaging company under the YAGEO Group, said its board has approved the acquisition of a 100% stake in Singapore-listed Global Testing Corporation for approximately SGD76.71 million (US$59.88 million). title: Laster Tech posts third-quarter loss as shortages delay shipments
snippet: Taiwanese LED automotive lighting module maker Laster Tech reported a net loss of NT$150 million in the third quarter of 2026, as component shortages disrupted production schedules and left shipments below expectations. title: Global smartphone revenue rises despite sharp shipment decline
snippet: Global smartphone revenue rose 3% year on year to US$114 billion in the third quarter of 2026, even as shipments fell 19%, highlighting a worldwide shift toward more expensive devices. Higher prices supported value, but rising memory costs are squeezing manufacturers' margins and threatening affordability, especially in entry-level markets worldwide.

title: AI boom drives photomask outsourcing despite IP fears, Tekscend says
snippet: Memory chipmakers have long been reluctant to outsource sensitive photomask production over intellectual property concerns, but growing artificial intelligence (AI) demand and capacity constraints are pushing more work to merchant suppliers, according to Japan's Tekscend Photomask. Manufacturers are keeping their most advanced extreme ultraviolet (EUV) masks in-house while outsourcing more conventional photomasks.

title: Taiwan begins 6G spectrum prep as 4G licenses expire in 2030
snippet: Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs (MODA) plans to begin preparatory work in 2027 for a potential 6G spectrum release, as licenses for the 700MHz, 900MHz, and 1800MHz bands are due to expire at the end of 2030. The ministry has said the schedule, frequencies, and method for any 6G licensing remain under study and have not been finalized.

snippet: Unmanned vehicle systems developer 7STARLAKE announced on November 6 that it will work with South Korean robotics company Raion Robotics and National Cheng Kung University (NCKU) to develop a physical AI and autonomous quadruped robot platform in Taiwan. The project will integrate multisensor data fusion, robot dynamics and terrain-contact simulations through virtual-physical closed-loop validation to strengthen local autonomy for unmanned vehicles.

snippet: Calls to curb artificial intelligence (AI) expansion have intensified after the US Democratic Party's sweeping victory in the midterm elections, but Trans-Sun Materials Technology Chairman Chia-Wang Li said political changes will not derail the AI growth trend. Regulatory measures under Democratic control could slightly delay some AI infrastructure projects, he said, but AI infrastructure remains an irreversible economic trend.

Revenue for the first 10 months reached NT$792.871 million, up 23.20% year-on-year and surpassing its full-year 2025 revenue of NT$782.351 million, highlighting continued momentum in its core businesses.

title: Taiwan telecom leader pledges more film, TV investment as OTT competition intensifies
snippet: Chunghwa Telecom (CHT) is expanding its investment in film and television content as competition in Taiwan's over-the-top (OTT) market intensifies. The Chunghwa Digital Cultural and Creative Fund (CDCCF), jointly backed by CHT, the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), and E.Sun Bank, began operations in 2026 and recently announced 10 new investments to broaden opportunities for Taiwan's film and television industry through funding, international co-production, and overseas partnerships.

title: Winbond sees AI data center buildout largely secured through 2028, flags 2029 as possible turning point
snippet: Winbond Electronics chairman Arthur Chiao said the AI data center buildout planned by major cloud service providers (CSPs) for 2027 and 2028 is largely secured, with funding, land, power, and infrastructure almost all in place, so there is no need to worry too much about investment freezing in the near term. But 2029 could become a key point for the next downturn, when it remains to be seen whether funding can keep supporting such massive spending, he said.

title: Winbond to run Infineon flash unit as independent, fabless Spansion brand
snippet: Winbond Electronics will revive the Spansion brand for the NOR Flash and F-RAM business it is buying from Infineon Technologies and run it as a fully independent, fabless company, chairman Arthur Chiao said, describing the US$1.12 billion deal as a way to secure top international talent and intellectual property.

title: Fino raises capital again to dilute Chinese ownership, meet US PFE rules
snippet: Fino, a South Korean company backed by Chinese precursor producer CNGR Advanced Material, will raise about KRW183 billion (approximately US$130 million) through a cash capital increase to fund its lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials business. The move is widely viewed as another step to reduce Chinese ownership and comply with the US Prohibited Foreign Entity (PFE) rules.

title: Agility Robotics lists on Nasdaq, faces profit test despite US$300 million order
snippet: Agility Robotics listed on Nasdaq on November 5, becoming the first publicly traded US humanoid robot maker and a key benchmark for assessing the sector’s commercial value. The company raised approximately US$465 million through the listing, but continues to face significant losses during its early commercialization phase.

title: Phison Electronics' AI business tops 50% of revenue in 3Q26
snippet: Phison Electronics' AI business contributed more than 50% of total revenue in the third quarter of 2026, as demand for AI infrastructure and enterprise storage continued to grow. The company reported record revenue, gross profit, and earnings per share (EPS) for the period, and is targeting continued growth in all three financial metrics through its Phison 3.0 strategy.

title: Taiwanese engineering company Yankey holds NT$57.1 billion orders, Kumamoto wafer fab project to boost 2027 revenue
snippet: Yankey Engineering’s order backlog reached a record NT$57.1 billion (US$1.74 billion) as of the end of September, with its subcontracting project for the second wafer fab in Kumamoto, Japan, expected to contribute revenue from 2027. The company said strong global AI infrastructure demand, advanced semiconductor processes, advanced packaging, and memory expansion drove its revenue and profit to record levels in the first three quarters of 2026.

title: Intel targets silicon photonics, in-memory computing beyond GPUs
snippet: As the global semiconductor industry continues to focus on Nvidia, Intel is looking beyond GPUs to determine where next-generation computing architectures will go. In an interview with Japanese publication PC Watch, Intel chief technology officer Pushkar Ranade outlined the company's technology roadmap, spanning advanced process technology, AI accelerators, quantum computing, neuromorphic computing, silicon photonics, in-memory computing, and new materials.

title: Exclusive: influx of Chinese capital drives gallium oxide substrate price cuts toward 2027
snippet: Gallium oxide (Ga2O3), a compound ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor material, is poised to hit a critical turning point in 2027. Semiconductor supply chain sources indicate that market attention is currently focused on whether substrate prices will reduce past historical trends. Notably, select material suppliers have already signaled to customers that larger price cuts are on the horizon, drawing keen industry interest.

title: Winbond chairman urges restraint in memory rally, expects 30-month bonuses as Nuvoton plans succession
snippet: Winbond Electronics chairman Arthur Chiao said memory prices and profits should not go any further at this stage, warning that a market in which memory thrives while other industries struggle is bad for consumers and the wider economy.

title: ePaper manufacturer E Ink to buy manufacturing plant in Taiwan for NT$2.78 billion, teams with Taiflex on AI materials
snippet: E Ink Holdings' board on November 6 approved buying land and factory buildings in Taoyuan's Guanyin Industrial Park from Chung Hwa Pulp for NT$2.78 billion (US$84.63 million) before tax, and signed off on a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Taiflex Scientific to jointly target the market for AI high-speed transmission materials.

title: Singapore fab set to drive VIS growth as AI interposers reshape output
snippet: Vanguard International Semiconductor (VIS) said its Singapore wafer fab is expected to become a growth driver in 2027, with capacity nearly sold out, customer commitments secured, and artificial-intelligence interposers projected to generate about half of revenue. The expansion could accelerate, but rising depreciation and fixed costs are expected to pressure profitability.

title: AI demand points to tighter capacity, higher prices at Taiwanese foundry service Vanguard
snippet: Vanguard International Semiconductor expects utilization of its 8-inch mature-node fabs to exceed 90% in the fourth quarter of 2026, as AI data center demand lifts orders for power management ICs and power components. The forecast points to tighter capacity, higher prices, and a growing role for AI revenue in its business.

title: Research Insight: FIT expands liquid cooling connector lineup for Vera Rubin NVL72
snippet: Foxconn Interconnect Technology (FIT) is expanding its lineup of liquid-cooling quick-disconnect (QD) connectors for Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, offering connections at both the server tray and rack levels. The company is incorporating blind-mate and floating connector mechanisms to reduce manual alignment during equipment installation and maintenance as it pursues opportunities in the next generation of AI data center (AIDC) liquid cooling.

title: South Korea plans first orbital AI data center test for 2028
snippet: South Korea plans to develop small, medium, and large data centers in orbit under its K-Moonshot initiative, aiming to conduct its first in-orbit demonstration in 2028 and lay the groundwork for commercial space-based AI services before 2035.

title: Infineon bets on 800V DC for megawatt AI racks
snippet: Rising power demand at AI data centers is driving demand for power semiconductors used in server power supplies, grid equipment, and chip-level power delivery. Infineon Technologies is positioning its silicon (Si), silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) portfolio for a shift toward 800V DC architectures, solid-state transformers and vertical power delivery, addressing different voltage, power and efficiency requirements as it expands its AI infrastructure business.

title: Japanese chipmaker Rapidus targets Taiwan’s chip cluster model, plans 3 more Hokkaido plants
snippet: Rapidus President Atsuyoshi Koike said the Japanese chipmaker will use Taiwan as a model for building a semiconductor industry cluster in Hokkaido, while IBM Japan is establishing a new office near Rapidus’ plant to strengthen support for the company.

title: Horngyu targets global grid market with AI, power integration
snippet: Global AI data center construction and Taiwan Power's NT$564.5 billion (US$17.23 billion) resilient-grid initiative are driving demand for highly reliable power equipment and intelligent management. Smart-power provider Horngyu Electric is integrating hardware and software to capture opportunities in the global power-grid market.

title: Automotive component maker PMX doubles semiconductor revenue share to 20%
snippet: Automotive powertrain and safety component maker Global PMX reported 3Q26 consolidated revenue of NT$2.417 billion (US$73.76 million), up 5.87% quarter-on-quarter and 24.59% year-on-year. Stronger operating scale and tight cost controls lifted quarterly operating profit to NT$340 million, while net income attributable to the parent company reached NT$271 million, with earnings per share (EPS) of NT$2.36.

title: Infineon, Solum expand cooperation on HVDC power for AI data centers
snippet: Infineon Technologies and Solum have agreed to expand cooperation on high-voltage direct current (HVDC) power systems for artificial intelligence data centers, as rising computing demand increases pressure on operators worldwide to improve efficiency, power density, and reliability. The partnership will cover intermediate bus converters, battery backup units, and power supply units.

title: Seoul court rejects LG Chem bid to halt Ronbay unit's cathode output, report says
snippet: A Seoul court has dismissed LG Chem's request for a preliminary injunction that would have halted production and sales of certain cathode materials by JS Energy, the South Korean subsidiary of Chinese cathode maker Ronbay, The Elec reported on November 7, citing industry sources. LG Chem has appealed.

title: India approves INR75 billion in electronics projects, expanding materials production
snippet: India approved 12 applications involving a proposed investment of INR75.03 billion (US$796.90 million) under its Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) on November 6, broadening support for domestic materials and manufacturing equipment. The projects are expected to generate production worth INR390.45 billion and create 7,127 direct jobs, the electronics ministry said.
